sections.h2: What should a seller in Clearwater know first?
sections.html:
Owners in Clearwater can list with an agent, handle a sale alone, or take a cash purchase. Which one fits turns on the shape of the house, the calendar and whatever loan or tenant comes with it. QuickFacts shows 114,364 residents for July 2025, a drop of 2.5% from the April 2020 estimate base.

A shrinking headcount means the pool of local buyers is not swelling. Residents 65 and over make up 24.1% of the city, so downsizing moves and estate sales make up a good part of the activity. Those sellers frequently prefer an as-is deal over a round of repairs.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about housing in Clearwater?
sections.html:
A typical owner-occupied Clearwater home was valued at $361,300 for 2020 through 2024, and just 58.6% of housing is lived in by its owner. That leaves a big rental share, so plenty of sellers here are landlords with tenants inside.

  • Households: 49,998, at 2.27 persons each.
  • Gross rent, median: $1,658 monthly.
  • Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,908 monthly; owners without one pay $811.
  • Land: 26.08 square miles, roughly 4,497 residents per square mile at the 2020 count.
  • Drive to work: 22.7 minutes on average.

The gap between $1,908 and $811 shows that many owners have cleared their loans and sell with a large share of equity.

sections.h2: What drives the Clearwater economy that buyers come from?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists 2022 receipts for three sectors that show where local jobs sit. Health care and social assistance took in $2,141,477 thousand, accommodation and food services $974,190 thousand, and transportation and warehousing $453,408 thousand, while retail sales reached $4,429,194 thousand, or $37,855 per resident.

Health care is the largest of the three. Among people 16 and older, 59.3% are in the labor force, and 32.6% of adults aged 25 and up have a bachelor's degree. A seller can use those facts to speak to the buyers likely to view the house: working households with a commute near 23 minutes, and retirees.

sections.h2: Can a Clearwater landlord sell a rental house?
sections.html:
Yes. The city's Planning and Development Department publishes a Business Tax Receipt application for residential rentals, and it spells out what Clearwater expects of a rental. The form defines a residential use inside a residential zoning district excludes stays under 31 days or one calendar month, whichever is less.

An owner who rents by the night should read that wording before listing, since a buyer planning short stays will ask. The form also names the housing code items an inspector can review:

  • Kitchen sink, stove and refrigerator, plus bath fixtures and hot and cold water.
  • Heating, smoke detectors and fire protection.
  • Windows, ventilation and lighting in halls and stairways.
  • Electrical outlets and lights.
  • Walls, roofs, ceilings and floors, checked for leaks.
  • Stairs, porches, doors, and pest control.

It also requires a local property manager with a street address in Pinellas, Hillsborough, Pasco, Manatee or Sarasota County. Before a rental changes hands, ask Planning and Development about the current fee and the registration steps for the new owner.

sections.h2: What does Clearwater's code say about the outside of a house?
sections.html:
The same application lists exterior standards that code officers apply to any residential lot: abandoned vehicles, address numbers, debris, sound fences, graffiti, overgrown grass, outdoor storage, parking, lighting and trash facilities.

Walk the lot with that list before the first showing. A boat parked on the grass or a tall lawn can draw a complaint mid-sale, and a buyer's inspector will write up the same items. Fixing them is cheap next to a price reduction.

sections.h2: Which Pinellas County office handles value and exemptions for a Clearwater home?
sections.html:
The county property appraiser sets values, and the main office sits at 315 Court Street, 2nd floor, Clearwater, open 8 AM to 5 PM on weekdays. Its homepage counts 437,624 real property parcels, among them 408,947 residential parcels, 103,445 condo units and 44,323 manufactured home units.

Those counts show how often a Clearwater sale involves a condo or a manufactured home, each with separate paperwork. On the state's calendar, values are set as of January 1, exemption filings are due March 1, and proposed values arrive in the August TRIM notice. After a sale, a homestead is revalued at full just value starting the next January 1, because the sale counts as a change of ownership.

sections.h2: How are Florida taxes handled when a Clearwater house sells?
sections.html:
On a Pinellas deed the state charges 70 cents for every $100 of the price. The statute makes each signer answerable, whichever one the contract names as payer, and the clerk takes payment at recording. Find that line on the settlement statement before you sign anything.

Tax bills are mailed in November. Paying in November earns a 4 percent discount, December 3 percent, January 2 percent and February 1 percent, and anything unpaid goes delinquent on April 1. If you close partway through the year, the title company prorates the bill with the buyer, so ask for its method.

sections.h2: What if a Clearwater owner is behind on the mortgage?
sections.html:
Foreclosure in Florida goes through a judge. The clerk schedules the auction between 20 and 35 days after the final judgment, though the lender may agree to a later date, and the winning bidder leaves a 5 percent deposit. If the house sells before that date, the loan is paid out of the proceeds and the case can close.

The certificate of title that follows an auction triggers deed tax measured on the top bid. Call your loan servicer or a Florida attorney soon, and set a cash offer beside a short sale before an auction date arrives.

sections.h2: What should a seller of an inherited Clearwater home do?
sections.html:
Settle who has authority first, because heirs cannot convey clean title on their own. An estate worth $150,000 or less in non-exempt assets can use summary administration, and so can one where more than two years have passed since the death. The Department of Revenue treats a personal representative's deed under a probated will as exempt from deed tax.

Creditors lose their claims unless they file within three months of the first published notice, or 30 days after being served if that is later. Florida levies no estate tax on deaths after 2004. The probate court clerk can say which path applies to this estate.

faqs.q: Is a cash sale in Clearwater faster than listing?
faqs.a: Closing can come within days or weeks, since no lender or appraisal stands in the way. A listing adds showings, repair negotiations and loan timelines. Compare what you would net on each path before choosing.

faqs.q: Does Clearwater require a permit or inspection to sell?
faqs.a: No city permit is required merely to sell. Open permits and code violations can still hold up a closing, so ask Planning and Development to check your address. A rental also needs its Business Tax Receipt dealt with.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Clearwater house with tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. A sale does not cancel the lease by itself. Florida allows 3 days' written notice for unpaid rent and requires 30 days to end a tenancy that runs month to month, so the buyer either keeps the tenant or waits out proper notice.

faqs.q: Who pays deed tax on a Clearwater sale?
faqs.a: By statute every signer of the deed answers for it, and contracts usually put it on the seller. The state rate is 70 cents per $100. Check the allocation in your contract and on the settlement statement.

faqs.q: Where do I check my Clearwater homestead status?
faqs.a: Ask the Pinellas County Property Appraiser. New exemption filings are due March 1, and homestead ends if the home is rented or stops being your permanent residence.
